stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking of a significant open-source LLM.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is categorized under key AI/ML tags like 'transformers' and 'llama', signifying its relevance in the open-source AI community.

stories.title: Anthropic will design its own hardware to power Claude
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Anthropic is developing custom hardware to support its Claude AI models.
This move signals a strategic effort by major AI labs to reduce reliance on Nvidia GPUs.
The development highlights the intense industry race to scale AI capabilities independently.

stories.title: Large genome models used to design new viruses
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Large genome models are being utilized in synthetic biology to design novel viruses.
The AI system is capable of generating genetically diverse variants of existing bacteria-killing viruses.
This research represents a significant intersection of advanced AI/ML and virology/biotechnology.

stories.title: AMD acquires Taalas to boost inference performance by etching models in silicon
stories.author: itvision
bullet_points: AMD acquired Taalas to enhance performance specifically for AI inference workloads.
The core technology involves 'etching models in silicon,' suggesting hardware-level optimization for AI.
This move targets the rapidly expanding market for AI inference solutions.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function in generative AI.
Relevant technologies mentioned include transformers and safetensors, placing it within the modern LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and multi-token prediction (MTP).
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also delivers faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware, emphasizing privacy.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, leveraging Apple's native ML framework.
This represents a significant step toward faster, on-device AI inference on Apple hardware.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The core value proposition is connecting communication tools directly to local, private AI capabilities.

stories.title: OpenAI is giving ChatGPT free users unlimited text chats
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: OpenAI is removing rate limits for text chats on free and Go tiers of ChatGPT.
This change significantly improves the usability and accessibility of the chatbot for general users.
The update is scheduled to roll out starting next week.

stories.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
stories.author: Nuno Vasconcelos
bullet_points: Introduces a novel method for On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPD/OSPD) in Large Language Models (LLMs).
Addresses a key limitation of existing methods by achieving self-distillation without relying on external supervision (ground-truth or external guidance).
Leverages the model's own generations and internal consistency to drive the distillation process.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now supported via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Jony Ive’s first OpenAI gadget is reportedly a hockey puck-sized smart speaker
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: OpenAI is collaborating with Jony Ive on a new AI gadget.
The device is described as a battery-powered, puck-sized smart speaker without a display.
It is anticipated to launch in 2027 with a price point exceeding $300.

stories.title: Suno shares plans to combat spammy AI music
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Suno is implementing watermarking technology to combat the spread of spammy AI music.
The company is also introducing a new download policy to enhance transparency.
The move reflects Suno's strategy to increase legitimacy within the AI music industry.

stories.title: Brendan Carr officially unleashes broadcast consolidation
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: The FCC has voted to eliminate the national broadcast ownership cap rule.
This decision allows for greater consolidation among broadcast station owners.
The vote was driven by FCC Republicans, including Chair Brendan Carr.

stories.title: Suno hopes to go legit with watermarks for AI-generated music
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Suno, an AI music generator, is implementing watermarks on its output.
The primary goal of these measures is to combat 'large-scale abuse' of the AI tool.
Download limits are also being introduced as part of the strategy to control misuse.

stories.title: Blue Origin narrowing in on root cause of catastrophic rocket accident
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Blue Origin is investigating the cause of a recent rocket accident.
The investigation has narrowed the anomaly to the main oxygen valve.
The issue was found on one of the BE-4 engines.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simply training models to ignore all context.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark designed to test reasoning under various context conditions (clean, misleading, etc.).

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes a large portion of data scientists' time.
The focus is on heart failure, a major health issue requiring complex integration of fragmented EHR data with clinical guidelines.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by offering more comprehensive and maintainable automation for feature extraction.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a new method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional evaluation methods by allowing for certified anytime-valid stopping.
Claims to achieve up to 74x cost reduction in agent evaluation while maintaining statistical guarantees.

stories.title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: Video Language Models struggle with granular event bookkeeping (e.g., counting specific actions).
Current benchmarks are flawed because they conflate event count, rate, and visual complexity within fixed clips.
The paper introduces 'trace-grounded parametric profiling' to provide fine-grained auditing of reported events against ground truth.

stories.title: Challenges in Evaluating Explanation Methods for Static and Evolving Data
stories.author: Jerzy Stefanowski
bullet_points: The paper addresses critical limitations in the evaluation of Explainable AI (XAI) methods.
It demonstrates issues using the DetoxAI system for bias detection and concept unlearning in image recognition.
The research explores adapting explanations, such as counterfactuals, to handle evolving data streams and concept drift.

stories.title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
stories.author: Juanzi Li
bullet_points: Introduces TRAJDEBUG, a method designed to trace the error lifecycle in complex, long-horizon agent trajectories.
Addresses the critical challenge of cascading errors and debugging difficulties inherent in LLM-based agentic systems.
Focuses on identifying the earliest error step responsible for a final failure, despite evidence being scattered across long sequences.

stories.title: Tytan: Interactive Neurosymbolic Construction of Analytic Semantic Schemas from Relational Data
stories.author: Kristian J. Hammond
bullet_points: Introduces TYTAN, a system designed to automatically construct analytic semantic schemas from raw relational data.
Addresses the 'knowledge-acquisition bottleneck' where semantic layers are currently manually created, limiting scalability and user accessibility.
Aims to improve data analysis tools by enabling natural-language querying and automated report generation without manual expert intervention.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of large language models (LLMs) to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark designed to test context reliability under various conditions.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The research addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes a large portion of data scientists' time.
The focus is specifically on heart failure, requiring the integration of fragmented EHR data with complex, guideline-based clinical reasoning.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by providing evidence-linked and more maintainable feature engineering.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a new method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of current evaluation methods by providing a certified anytime-valid stopping criterion.
Claims to reduce the cost of agent evaluation by a factor of 74 compared to existing approaches.

stories.title: CalibForge: Adversarial Solver Calibration for Scaling Learnable Terminal Tasks
stories.author: Kai Jia
bullet_points: Introduces CalibForge, an autonomous system for synthesizing terminal tasks in AI.
The system uses adversarial solver calibration to ensure tasks are appropriately challenging for learning, beyond mere solvability.
Addresses the gap between task feasibility (executable validation) and task difficulty relative to a specific solver.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in applying generative reward models (GRMs) to Reinforcement Learning (RL).
The core issue identified is the mismatch between GRMs' comparative nature and RL algorithms' scalar scoring requirement.
The authors propose a novel method (RRC) to bridge this gap and unlock GRMs' potential in LLM RL.

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: Focuses on the 'harness' (prompts, tools, orchestration) surrounding Large Language Models (LLMs) as a critical factor in performance, not just the model weights.
Introduces the concept of automated harness optimization, where an AI iteratively improves the surrounding system using evaluation feedback.
Highlights a current gap in the research community: the lack of a common protocol for measuring and benchmarking these harness optimizations.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simply training models to ignore all context.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark designed to test context-dependent reasoning under various conditions.

stories.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
stories.author: Vamse Kumar Subbiah
bullet_points: The paper investigates Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC) as an evolution of LLM tool use, moving beyond rigid JSON calls to allow for natural scripting and parallelization.
PTC enables LLMs to function as more capable agents that can execute actions outside their initial training data.
The research addresses a gap by empirically comparing PTC against native JSON tool calling on established benchmarks under real-world conditions.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the high cost and uncertainty of traditional agent comparison methods.
Provides a certified anytime-valid stopping criterion, ensuring evaluation accuracy without fixed budgets.

stories.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
stories.author: Shujian Huang
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of multilingual reasoning transfer in Large Language Models (LLMs) beyond high-resource languages.
It introduces RP-OPSD, a novel method that enhances On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) by explicitly guiding the distillation process with reasoning signals.
The core contribution is characterizing the components of target-language reasoning necessary for effective cross-lingual transfer.

stories.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
stories.author: Abigail Goldsteen
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in NLP: the lack of quality assessment for conversational agent benchmarks.
Proposes a novel, reference-free framework utilizing LLM judges to evaluate benchmark consistency, complexity, and policy coverage.
Aims to provide actionable diagnostics to improve the reliability of evaluating task-oriented conversational agents.

stories.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
stories.author: Tianyong Hao
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in evaluating LLMs for complex, rule-intensive document review tasks.
National standard documents (e.g., China GB/T) are proposed as a rigorous testbed due to their length, structure, and explicit rules.
Current LLM benchmarks are criticized for focusing too much on domain knowledge and Q&A, neglecting intrinsic structural compliance.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in LLM Reinforcement Learning (RL) by focusing on generative reward models.
It identifies a core limitation: the mismatch between generative models' comparative nature and RL's scalar scoring requirement.
The authors propose a method (RRC) to bridge this gap, enabling generative reward models to be effectively used in RL.

stories.title: Beyond Top-K: Replacing Black-Box Retrieval with Interpretable Agentic Operations
stories.author: Tabarakul Hazarika
bullet_points: The paper critiques the standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach (chunking and top-K retrieval) for long documents.
It argues that the standard RAG design is structurally unsound for complex, structured documents like financial statements and regulatory reports.
The research proposes replacing black-box retrieval with more interpretable, agentic operations to handle document complexity.

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in agentic systems is heavily dependent on the surrounding 'harness' (prompts, tools, control flow, etc.), not just the model weights.
Automated harness optimization—using AI to iteratively improve the surrounding code/prompts—is identified as a critical, yet challenging, area for AI advancement.
The research addresses a lack of a common protocol within the community for measuring and evaluating these harness optimization techniques.

stories.title: I Spent a Day With Kiro Crew. Here's What It Actually Does.
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: Demonstrates an AI agent's capability to autonomously investigate and resolve production issues (P1 latency spikes).
Highlights the practical application of AI in DevOps/SRE, specifically for automated incident response and prevention.
Presents a low operational cost model ($0.04 per incident) for this advanced automation.
